mechanism_narrative: The continued week-over-week recovery in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT signals more daytime trips and foot traffic, which should raise RETAIL_REC over the next month as commuting-linked visits spill into shopping and dining.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve relative to the last 4 weeks even though WORKPLACES and TRANSIT keep rising for two more weekly observations.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL remains elevated while WORKPLACES stay subdued, people substitute local errands and nearby leisure for longer trips, which lifts neighborhood retail visits faster than destination retail and pushes RETAIL_REC up within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL stays above 5 points while WORKPLACES stays below -15 points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise within 14 days despite RESIDENTIAL staying above 5 and WORKPLACES remaining below -15.

mechanism_narrative: A renewed drop in TRANSIT below its current depressed level will cut access to city-center retail and suppress discretionary shopping visits, so RETAIL_REC will fall over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -55 after having been above -52 the prior week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises or stays flat over the next 28 days after TRANSIT crosses back below -55.

mechanism_narrative: An improvement in PARKS relative to its recent trough indicates better weather and outdoor activity, which usually diverts demand toward non-retail recreation and leaves RETAIL_REC weaker over the following week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by at least 5 points from the prior week after a prior two-week decline
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not weaken in the next 7 days after PARKS rebounds by at least 5 points.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM is stable or slightly positive while PARKS are soft, routine shopping trips dominate discretionary outings and support broader retail demand, producing a modest rise in RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to outperform the prior 4-week average even though GROCERY_PHARM stays nonnegative and PARKS remain negative.

mechanism_narrative: A continued decline in WORKPLACES from the recent improvement signals that mobility gains are stalling, which should quickly reduce incidental shopping trips and pull RETAIL_REC lower within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES reverses by falling more than 3 points week-on-week after a weekly rise
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline within 14 days after WORKPLACES turns down by more than 3 points week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: Under reopening conditions, simultaneous recovery in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES creates a compounding commute-and-lunch effect that expands retail footfall and pushes RETAIL_REC higher over four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains below the prior 4-week mean even as TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both rise for at least two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If PARKS stay depressed while RESIDENTIAL stays elevated, people are staying local but not shifting toward discretionary outings, so retail demand weakens and RETAIL_REC drifts down over the next month.
candidate_trigger: PARKS remains below -10 and RESIDENTIAL remains above 5 for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days despite PARKS staying below -10 and RESIDENTIAL staying above 5.
